# DiscoveryEngineCmekConfig

`discoveryengine.gcp.hfl.dev/v1alpha1`

**Gap it fills.** Terraform's `google_discovery_engine_cmek_config`. A Cloud KMS key that Vertex AI Search (Discovery Engine) encrypts a location's data with; location is us or eu, served at that location's host. The API has no create: patch makes the config. Terraform's set_default defaults to true; here setDefault is sent only when the spec sets it.

**Source.** generated by `hack/discokind` from the discoveryengine.v1 Discovery document.

## Notes

Generated by `hack/discokind` from `hack/discokind/kinds.yaml` (`docs/design.md`
section 2.4); its test is `pkg/discokind/kindtest` with the fixtures under
`pkg/controller/direct/discoveryengine/testdata/discokind/DiscoveryEngineCmekConfig/`.

The API has no create method: `cmekConfigs.patch` (no update mask, a
long-running operation) makes a config and changes it, so the controller
patches the spec's whole body for both (`PatchCreates`). `us` and `eu` are
served at `https://us-discoveryengine.googleapis.com/` and
`https://eu-discoveryengine.googleapis.com/` (`locationHost`).
`setDefault` is patch's query parameter, sent with every write; the API
never returns it, so changing it alone does not write (the config's
`status.observedState.isDefault` says whether it is the default).

Live: skipped (`live-skip`). It needs `discoveryengine.googleapis.com` on
in the test project and a Cloud KMS key in the `us` multi-region that the
project's Discovery Engine service agent
(`service-<number>@gcp-sa-discoveryengine.iam.gserviceaccount.com`) holds
`roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` on; the live tests may not
enable APIs or grant IAM. What the fake cannot show is in
`docs/fake-cloud.md`.
